title: Your tools, ready to go
say: Welcome back! Keep your pencils beside you: 2H or HB for light construction lines, then 2B and 3B for the deeper tones. Have your tissue and eraser nearby, and set out your sketch paper. Today we draw a real apple.

captions.text: Welcome back! Keep your pencils beside you: 2H
or HB for light construction lines, then 2B
and 3B for the deeper tones. Have your
tissue and eraser nearby, and set out your
sketch paper. Today we draw a real apple.

title: Set your stage
say: Set your apple where you can see it clearly, with light coming from one side only. One light means one highlight, one shadow side, and one cast shadow. That is all we need to make the apple look round.

captions.text: Set your apple where you can see it clearly,
with light coming from one side only. One light
means one highlight, one shadow side, and one cast
shadow. That is all we need to make the
apple look round.

title: Look before you draw
say: Before you draw, look. A real apple is not a perfect ball. One side is a little fuller, the top dips in where the stem sits. Find what makes your apple different from a plain sphere. That difference is the character of your drawing.

captions.text: Before you draw, look. A real apple is
not a perfect ball. One side is a
little fuller, the top dips in where the
stem sits. Find what makes your apple different
from a plain sphere. That difference is the
character of your drawing.

title: Watch the demo
say: Watch my demonstration once, all the way through. Do not draw yet. Notice the order: light lines first, tones later, darkest accents last. When you know the whole journey, each step feels easy.

captions.text: Watch my demonstration once, all the
way through. Do not draw yet.
Notice the order: light lines first,
tones later, darkest accents last. When
you know the whole journey, each
step feels easy.

title: Where is the light?
say: Find where the light comes from. The brightest spot on the apple, the highlight, sits on the light side. Point at it with your pencil. Everything we shade grows out from this one decision.

captions.text: Find where the light comes from. The brightest
spot on the apple, the highlight, sits on
the light side. Point at it with your
pencil. Everything we shade grows out from this
one decision.

title: Meet the shadow side
say: Now find the shadow side, opposite the light. The darkest band, the core shadow, hugs the round form right where the surface turns away from the light. Squint your eyes, and the big shapes become obvious.

captions.text: Now find the shadow side, opposite the light. The
darkest band, the core shadow, hugs the round form
right where the surface turns away from the light.
Squint your eyes, and the big shapes become obvious.

title: The shadow on the table
say: Look at the table. The apple throws a soft shadow to one side. Notice it is darkest near the apple and fades as it moves away. We will draw it later, but we plan for it now.

captions.text: Look at the table. The apple throws a soft
shadow to one side. Notice it is darkest near
the apple and fades as it moves away. We
will draw it later, but we plan for it
now.

title: Measure with your pencil
say: Take your 2H pencil and hold it up with a straight arm. Measure the apple's height, then compare it to the width. Is it a little wider than it is tall? Lock that proportion in your mind before any line goes down.

captions.text: Take your 2H pencil and hold it up with a
straight arm. Measure the apple's height, then compare it to
the width. Is it a little wider than it is
tall? Lock that proportion in your mind before any line
goes down.

title: Frame it lightly
say: Lightly frame the apple: one vertical line for height, one horizontal line for width. Keep your touch feather-light. These are thinking lines. They will melt into the drawing later.

captions.text: Lightly frame the apple: one vertical line
for height, one horizontal line for width.
Keep your touch feather-light. These are thinking
lines. They will melt into the drawing
later.

title: Find the lean
say: Mark the vertical center. A real apple leans a little. It is rarely perfectly symmetrical. Let your center line lean the way your apple leans.

captions.text: Mark the vertical center. A real apple leans
a little. It is rarely perfectly symmetrical. Let
your center line lean the way your apple
leans.

title: Mark the widest points
say: Mark the widest points on both sides. Check with your pencil: is the left side fuller than the right? Adjust until the two sides feel like your apple, not just any apple.

captions.text: Mark the widest points on both sides. Check
with your pencil: is the left side fuller
than the right? Adjust until the two sides
feel like your apple, not just any apple.

title: Draw the round contour
say: Now connect the marks with a round, confident contour, still with the light 2H. Go around twice if you like. The second pass always understands the form better than the first.

captions.text: Now connect the marks with a round,
confident contour, still with the light 2H.
Go around twice if you like. The
second pass always understands the form better
than the first.

title: The little dip on top
say: Draw the little dip at the top where the stem sits. It is a small curve, but it tells everyone this is an apple and not a ball. Take your time here.

captions.text: Draw the little dip at the top where the stem
sits. It is a small curve, but it tells everyone
this is an apple and not a ball. Take your
time here.

title: Place the stem
say: Add the stem with two short lines, tilted the way it grows from the dip. Keep it light for now. We will give it its tones later.

captions.text: Add the stem with two short lines, tilted the
way it grows from the dip. Keep it light
for now. We will give it its tones later.

title: Stop and compare
say: Stop and compare. Hold your drawing beside the apple, or step back three steps. Does the shape feel right? Fix the big shape now. Small details can wait.

captions.text: Stop and compare. Hold your drawing beside
the apple, or step back three steps.
Does the shape feel right? Fix the
big shape now. Small details can wait.

title: Change pencils: 2B
say: Time to change pencils. Put down the 2H and pick up the 2B. From here on, every tone stays visible, so work from light to dark, never the other way around.

captions.text: Time to change pencils. Put down the
2H and pick up the 2B. From
here on, every tone stays visible, so
work from light to dark, never the
other way around.

title: First tone: the shadow side
say: Lay a light, even tone over the whole shadow side, using the side of your 2B. Keep the highlight paper-white. Think of this as the first thin coat. We will build on it.

captions.text: Lay a light, even tone over the whole
shadow side, using the side of your 2B.
Keep the highlight paper-white. Think of this as
the first thin coat. We will build on
it.

title: Follow the roundness
say: Now the halftone, the middle area between highlight and shadow. Let your strokes follow the roundness of the apple, curving the way the surface curves. Straight strokes would flatten it.

captions.text: Now the halftone, the middle area between
highlight and shadow. Let your strokes follow
the roundness of the apple, curving the
way the surface curves. Straight strokes would
flatten it.

title: Deepen the core shadow
say: Deepen the core shadow, that dark band where the form turns away from the light. Press a little firmer with the 2B. This dark band is what makes the apple feel truly three-dimensional.

captions.text: Deepen the core shadow, that dark band where
the form turns away from the light. Press
a little firmer with the 2B. This dark
band is what makes the apple feel truly
three-dimensional.

title: Blend with tissue
say: Take your tissue and gently blend the tones. Small circles, light touch. Blending melts the pencil strokes into smooth skin, just like a real apple.

captions.text: Take your tissue and gently blend the tones.
Small circles, light touch. Blending melts the pencil
strokes into smooth skin, just like a real
apple.

title: Turn the form again
say: Look again. Where does the tone need to be darker to turn the form? Add another layer on the shadow side, always following the round direction. Patience builds volume.

captions.text: Look again. Where does the tone need to be
darker to turn the form? Add another layer on
the shadow side, always following the round direction. Patience
builds volume.

title: Tone the cast shadow
say: Now the cast shadow on the table. Use the side of the pencil. Keep the edge near the apple darker and let it fade outward. Soft edges here. There are no hard lines inside a shadow.

captions.text: Now the cast shadow on the table. Use the
side of the pencil. Keep the edge near the
apple darker and let it fade outward. Soft edges
here. There are no hard lines inside a shadow.

title: Change pencils: 3B
say: Switch to the 3B for the deepest darks. A 3B is rich and dark, so use it sparingly, only where you are completely sure.

captions.text: Switch to the 3B for the deepest darks.
A 3B is rich and dark, so use
it sparingly, only where you are completely sure.

title: The darkest accents
say: Place the darkest accents: deep in the dip around the stem, and the dark crease where the apple meets the table. These small darks make everything else in your drawing glow.

captions.text: Place the darkest accents: deep in the dip around the
stem, and the dark crease where the apple meets the
table. These small darks make everything else in your drawing
glow.

title: Shade the stem
say: Give the stem its tone: darker on the shadow side, a thin light edge on the light side. It is small, but it finishes the top of your apple.

captions.text: Give the stem its tone: darker on the shadow
side, a thin light edge on the light side.
It is small, but it finishes the top of
your apple.

title: A whisper of reflected light
say: Look closely at the very edge of the shadow side. There is a whisper of reflected light bouncing up from the table. Lift it gently with your eraser. Just a breath of light, nothing more.

captions.text: Look closely at the very edge of the
shadow side. There is a whisper of reflected
light bouncing up from the table. Lift it
gently with your eraser. Just a breath of
light, nothing more.

title: Unify the tones
say: Step back and squint. Do the tones flow from light to dark in one smooth journey? Soften any harsh jumps with the tissue. The whole apple should feel like one single round form.

captions.text: Step back and squint. Do the tones flow
from light to dark in one smooth journey?
Soften any harsh jumps with the tissue. The
whole apple should feel like one single round
form.

title: Final details
say: Final touches. Sharpen the stem's edge, clean the highlight with a careful eraser lift, and make sure the contour sits quietly inside the tones instead of shouting over them.

captions.text: Final touches. Sharpen the stem's edge, clean the highlight
with a careful eraser lift, and make sure the
contour sits quietly inside the tones instead of shouting
over them.

title: Step back
say: Put your pencil down and step back three steps. Compare your drawing with the apple. What is the one thing that would make it more convincing? Do that one thing, then stop.

captions.text: Put your pencil down and step back three steps. Compare
your drawing with the apple. What is the one thing
that would make it more convincing? Do that one thing,
then stop.

title: Sign your work
say: When it feels finished, sign your name small in a corner. You drew a real object with real light and shadow. That is no small thing.

captions.text: When it feels finished, sign your name small
in a corner. You drew a real object
with real light and shadow. That is no

title: Look at that roundness!
say: Look at that roundness! Your apple has real volume now. The sphere lessons are living inside this drawing.

captions.text: Look at that roundness! Your apple has real volume
now. The sphere lessons are living inside this drawing.

title: Trust the tones
say: The tones are building beautifully. Light to dark, patient layers. Trust the process. It is working.

captions.text: The tones are building beautifully. Light to dark,
patient layers. Trust the process. It is working.

title: Almost there
say: Almost there. The darkest accents are next, and they will make the whole apple sing.

captions.text: Almost there. The darkest accents are next,

title: Optional: a second apple
say: Optional challenge. Draw a second apple from a different angle, or cut one open and draw the inside. Same method, brand new adventure.

title: Optional: move the light
say: Try moving your light to the other side and draw the apple again in just five minutes. Notice how the whole drawing changes when the light moves.

captions.text: Try moving your light to the other side and

title: Share your apple
say: Photograph your apple drawing in good, even light, and submit it here. We would love to see your tones.

title: What did the light teach you?
say: What did you notice about light today that you never noticed before? Keep that question with you. It will follow you into every drawing you make.

captions.text: What did you notice about light today that

title: Lesson complete
say: Lesson complete. You built a real apple from light lines to full tones. Well done, artist.
